items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: And it was Frank Beach, the first trumpet—. this is what they needed. First trombone was Ray Cline, and a jazz clarinet player. So they asked three of us from the Les Brown band

ctx.x: It was one of the most gratifying, and I’m sorry to say nicest, supposed to be — in the military and I just had a ball because I learned how to write, how to arrange, and I learned how to play flute from one of the fellows in the band and it was great. There were great musicians from the west coast. That’s what enabled me to come out and go to Twentieth Century Fox. After the service, which was about three and a half years from ’42 to the

middle of ’45, I went back. Nothing much was happening, we did a little something and then I came back here and pretty soon — oh I went back with Tommy in ’46 — not back with Tommy, back with Les. Tommy was first. In ’46 my wife Gussie and I decided to get married and we were on the road for a year with Tommy Dorsey and then that would have been ’47, and then a little kidding around, I think we went back to New York for a while, then I went back with Les from about ’48 to ’50. And in ’50 these fellows that I had…
What was it like traveling on the road with a big band in those days?
